row.evidence: Spacelift's SCIM docs say "This feature is only available to Enterprise plan"; the pricing page lists Enterprise as "Request a quote" with "SSO integration with SAML 2.0".
row.notes: Flat platform pricing, not per user: Free (2 users), Starter+ $20,000 annual subscription with unlimited users, Business/Enterprise/Enterprise+ Request a quote, all with unlimited users. SCIM 2.0 (Users, Groups, discovery endpoints; OAuth 2.0 client credentials) and SAML are Enterprise-only; OIDC SSO is on any paid account per the SSO docs, so sso_plan is Starter+ (OIDC), while SAML is Enterprise. SCIM needs SSO configured first. SCIM does not assign permissions; roles are bound to SCIM groups via UI, Terraform or login policies, and group membership must also be sent on the login assertion. IdP deactivation deactivates the user and revokes sessions; delete hard-deletes and revokes sessions. The GraphQL API (all paid accounts per docs; API keys billed as users) has no documented user-management mutations in the docs; audit trail (log + webhook) is Enterprise-only.

auth.token_source: Organization Settings > Single Sign-On > SCIM > Activate (client ID and client secret, OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant)

deprovision.data_retained: On IdP deactivation the user record remains in Spacelift and can be reactivated if the IdP reprovisions the user; DELETE hard-deletes the user.
deprovision.notes: Admin docs say revoking access frees the seat on seat-limited plans (Free, Starter); SCIM is Enterprise-only, where users are unlimited (c41, c6).

custom.how: Custom schema extensions are listed as unsupported

roles.how: SCIM does not assign permissions and the roles attribute is ignored; roles are bound to SCIM-provisioned groups or users via the UI, the Terraform provider or login policies.

limitations.text: SCIM-provisioned users get no permissions; users without roles are denied at login.
Group-based authorization uses the groups sent on the SAML/OIDC login assertion, not SCIM-stored group membership.

Bulk operations, password changes, sorting and custom schema extensions are not supported; many optional core attributes (title, phoneNumbers, addresses, roles, entitlements, etc.) are silently ignored.
Okta does not expose SCIM on OIDC apps; Okta OIDC customers need a second SWA app for provisioning.
Under the Login Policy management strategy, deactivating a user in Spacelift does not block their login.

endpoints.purpose: Single GraphQL endpoint for all queries and mutations

audit_log_api.notes: Built-in audit log plus audit webhook delivery; Enterprise-only.

limitations.text: API keys are virtual users billed like regular users.

user_api.notes: The docs describe the GraphQL schema as self-documenting but do not document user-management queries or mutations, so capabilities are null. The plan for secret-based API keys is not stated.

okta.notes: Spacelift's Okta guide creates a custom app integration (Create App Integration), not an OIN app; okta.com/integrations/spacelift/ returned 404.

entra.notes: Spacelift documents Entra ID via an OIDC app registration plus generic SCIM; no Entra gallery tutorial found (learn.microsoft.com spacelift-tutorial 404).

onelogin.notes: Vendor docs name OneLogin for SCIM and have a OneLogin OIDC guide; catalogue listing not checked (OneLogin blocks bots).

fallbacks.other_sync: GitHub/GitLab/Google default login with login policies granting access by GitHub org/team membership

conflicts.text: The pricing page shows Free, Starter+, Business, Enterprise and Enterprise+ cards, while the pricing FAQ and admin docs refer to a seat-limited Starter plan that has no card.

open_questions: SCIM token/credential expiry is not documented.
SCIM rate limits are not documented.
GraphQL user-management mutations (invite, revoke, list users) are not documented in the docs; schema is self-documenting via introspection only.
Whether JIT user creation happens on first SSO login is not stated explicitly.
Whether Okta OIN, Entra gallery, Google, OneLogin or JumpCloud catalogue apps exist for Spacelift could not be confirmed (no web search available).
